scope: Woodford, Interest and Prices, Chapter 8: Optimal Policy Rules, with Appendix G. The general LQ setup and first-order conditions with the target-criterion construction via adjugates; Propositions 8.1-8.4 proved in general (Giannoni-Woodford theory the book does not prove): Prop 8.1 from Assumptions 8.2-8.4 via deflating subspaces of the pencil (1.15), corrected so multipliers are known at their date, with repeated roots and a normalisation-free case (ii); Prop 8.2 without a multiplier-stability hypothesis (Assumption 8.5 suffices) and with Assumption 8.1 corrected, robust optimality; Prop 8.3 superinertia with the no-circle hypothesis it needs (counterexample otherwise); Prop 8.4 unconditional; worked instances for the basic and inflation-inertia models. Optimal inflation targeting under inflation inertia, sticky wages (exact determinacy region for kappa_w /= kappa_p, with a counterexample), habit persistence, predetermined pricing, the Giannoni-Woodford model and imperfect information; Prop 8.5 determinacy for every admissible parameter and Prop 8.6; the inflation-inertia model: Prop 8.7 roots, Lemmas G.1-G.2, Prop 8.8 Rules I-III over the complex numbers with determinacy of the rule system, Props 8.9-8.11 unconditional with their limits, Figs 8.3-8.5 numbers (Fig 8.4 .39 enclosed). Book misprints and false claims are corrected with Lean counterexamples.
source: Michael Woodford, Interest and Prices: Foundations of a Theory of Monetary Policy, Princeton University Press, 2003, Chapter 8, pp. 534-623, and Appendix G, pp. 716-745; Giannoni and Woodford (2002a).
